Definition: Understandability refers to how easily developers can comprehend and maintain the test code.

Task: Improve the understandability of the test `TestInternationalFixedChronology_badLeapDayDates.java` (path:- /Users/tenghaha/Projects/New_Agent_understandability_improvement/data/original/threeten-extra/manual/testcases/TestInternationalFixedChronology/TestInternationalFixedChronology_badLeapDayDates.java). The refactored code must be syntactically correct and compilable against the provided CUT signatures. Do not alter the runtime behaviour of the original test: the same methods must be called with the same arguments and produce the same expected outcomes.

The original file is dominated by ~20 unused data-provider methods; only `data_badLeapDates` and the `badLeapDayDates` test actually run. Let me write a focused, readable version.Now I'll write a focused, readable version that preserves the exact runtime behavior:Compiles cleanly. I reduced the file from ~155 lines (dominated by ~20 unused data providers) to a focused test: removed all dead `data_*` methods, named the magic constants (`LEAP_MONTH`/`LEAP_DAY`), renamed the provider to `data_nonLeapYears` and the test to `of_leapDayInNonLeapYear_throws`, and documented *why* each year is non-leap — all while calling `InternationalFixedDate.of(year, 6, 29)` with the same arguments and expecting the same `DateTimeException`.
